title: Rh Alloimmunization: Screening and Fetal Risks
subject: OBG
preview: Rh alloimmunization occurs when maternal antibodies target fetal red-cell antigens inherited from the father.
quickRevision: Rh alloimmunization occurs when maternal antibodies target fetal red-cell antigens inherited from the father.
Anti-D immunoglobulin can prevent sensitization in eligible unsensitized RhD-negative patients according to local protocols.
Clinically significant alloantibodies may cause fetal anemia and neonatal hemolysis.

sections.title: Clinical syndrome and red flags
points: Rh alloimmunization occurs when maternal antibodies target fetal red-cell antigens inherited from the father.
Maternal antibody screening and blood-group typing guide monitoring and prophylaxis decisions.

sections.title: Differentiate and manage
points: Anti-D immunoglobulin can prevent sensitization in eligible unsensitized RhD-negative patients according to local protocols.
Clinically significant alloantibodies may cause fetal anemia and neonatal hemolysis.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Anti-D prophylaxis does not treat an already established immune anti-D response.

quiz.question: What is a major fetal risk of clinically significant red-cell alloimmunization?
options: Congenital cleft palate in every case
